intro.title: Write a custom once function utility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom utility function called `once` that ensures a given function can only be executed one time, no matter how many times it's called. You'll learn the core programming concept of closures, which allow a function to 'remember' and access variables from its outer scope even after that outer function has finished running. The main technologies and constructs involved are JavaScript functions, return statements, and boolean flags to track execution state. This is a practical exercise in writing reusable, efficient code that prevents side effects from repeated calls. By the end, you'll have a handy utility that can be applied in many real-world scenarios.
intro.usecase: The once function pattern is essential for preventing duplicate or repeated actions in user interfaces. For example, in a payment processing form, you would use it to ensure the 'Submit Order' button's click handler only executes once, even if a user clicks multiple times, preventing duplicate charges. It's also used in dashboard initialization to guarantee setup logic runs only a single time when the app loads, or in modal close handlers to avoid multiple cleanup calls. This utility helps developers enforce single execution in scenarios where repetition could cause errors, side effects, or degraded user experience.
